commitAtDiscovery: uncommitted working tree, branch phase-20-block-encoding (immediately after merging the Approach 1 / Engine Spec §6.2 sub-case iii-d Case C fix into engine.ts, discovered while building this project's OWN permanent regression fixtures for that fix)
oneLineDescription: A SECOND, structurally distinct gap in integrate(), same general shape as R0008 but in Case B (group inheritance) instead of Case C, discovered while validating R0008's fix. A wide-window candidate (originLeft=originRight=null) whose own scan encounters a node (t) anchored onto an ALREADY-RESOLVED-in-this-scan node (i) blindly inherits i's resolution for t via Case B's group-membership test, WITHOUT ever directly comparing rank(t) against rank(candidate) -- producing genuinely different, delivery-order-dependent VISIBLE TEXT ("ipt" vs "itp") with NO throw, NO canary, nothing catching it at all. Unlike R0008 (which threw loudly), this is a SILENT divergence -- arguably worse.
relationToR0008: Found via the SAME general principle R0008 established ("scan-window membership is not a sound proxy for safe-to-skip-by-rank"), but manifesting in a DIFFERENT branch (Case B's `conflicting`/`scanned` group-inheritance test, not Case C's now-fixed blind break). Discovered specifically because R0008's fix (Approach 1) closes the Case C path, which made it possible to build a PROPERLY VALIDATED (non-confounded) regression repro for R0008 -- and that validation work is what surfaced this second gap. Treated as the SAME investigation/emergency-priority item, not a new one, per explicit instruction.
discoveryNote: The first attempt at a 'corrected, distinct-replica-id' R0008 repro (p.r=5, i.r=1, t.r=3) was ITSELF flawed and accidentally vacuous: p.r=5 > t.r=3 means p never outranks t, so neither the original bug nor this one could ever manifest with those specific ids, regardless of which fix (if any) was applied -- it passed for the wrong reason. Caught by insisting on a PROPERLY validated relationship (i.r < p.r < t.r, chosen so Case A deterministically resolves p-vs-i with no tie, AND p genuinely outranks t) before treating any result as evidence. Verified pre-fix (Engine Spec §6.2 sub-case iii-d's original code) correctly throws the OLD canary on this validated repro (16/24, 85/120, 4/6 delivery orders across R0008/Q1/Q2 respectively) -- confirming the corrected repro is a real, non-vacuous regression test, not another accidental no-op.
harness: Same style as R0008: real Engine instances, hand-constructed Operation objects (not testkit's runTrial.ts), applied via applyRemote in every one of the 6 possible delivery-order permutations of the underlying 3 real operations (exhaustive, not sampled).

minimalReproduction.description: 3 real operations, distinct replica ids satisfying i.r=1 < p.r=2 < t.r=3 (this specific ordering is REQUIRED -- see discoveryNote and handTrace for why). Delivered via applyRemote in all 6 permutations to fresh Engine instances.
minimalReproduction.note: Deliberately simpler than R0008 -- no delete/tombstone at all (same as R0008's own Q2 variant, which already proved tombstoning is not load-bearing). This is the minimal shape that isolates Case B's gap specifically: p (wide-open window) must encounter BOTH i (a direct Case A competitor) AND t (anchored onto i, reached only via Case B) in the same scan.

postApproach1Behavior.description: Ran against engine.ts AFTER the Approach 1 / R0008 Case C fix was merged (the ORIGINAL canary/throw is gone, confirming that part of the fix works) -- but the underlying divergence is NOT closed.
postApproach1Behavior.result: 0/6 delivery orders throw. 2 distinct final structures across the 6 orders, collapsing into exactly 2 distinct VISIBLE TEXTS depending purely on whether 't' or 'p' is integrated first: delivering p before t converges (across all its own orderings) to "ipt"; delivering t before p converges to "itp". No assertion, canary, or invariant check catches this -- confirmed against Engine Spec's full I0-I9 invariant suite (assertInvariants raises nothing for either outcome, since both are individually well-formed structures; the violation is CROSS-replica, not detectable from a single replica's own state).
postApproach1Behavior.robustnessCheck: Confirmed not a coincidence of small numbers -- 5 different (i.r, p.r, t.r) combinations, all satisfying i.r < p.r < t.r, ALL produce the identical "ipt"/"itp" split: (1,2,3), (1,5,9), (2,4,100), (10,11,12), (1,50,51).

handTrace.orderA_pBeforeT: p integrates first (structure={i}): p's window is (null,null), spans the whole structure. Reaches i: Case A applies (both originLeft=null). compareRank(i,p) = 1-2 = -1 < 0 -> i outranks p -> destIndex advances past i, conflicting cleared. Result: [i,p]. Then t arrives, anchored originLeft=i (real): window is (i_pos+1, end), which now includes p. p.originLeft=null != t.originLeft=i -> not Case A. p.originLeft is ⊥ -> excluded from Case B (this IS the R0008 mechanism, now fixed) -> Case C (FIXED): compareRank(p,t) = 2-3 = -1 < 0 -> p outranks t -> destIndex advances past p. Final: [i,p,t] = "ipt".
handTrace.orderB_tBeforeP: t integrates first (structure={i}): t's window is (i_pos+1, end) = empty -> no conflict, inserted directly after i. Result: [i,t]. Then p arrives (window null,null, spans {i,t}): reaches i first, Case A, compareRank(i,p)=-1<0 -> i outranks p -> p's destIndex advances past i, conflicting.clear(). Continues scanning, reaches t next: t.originLeft=i (real, NOT null) -> not Case A (p.originLeft=null != t.originLeft=i). otherOriginKey = i's key. scanned.has(i's key) = TRUE (i was scanned earlier in THIS SAME p-integration pass) -> CASE B. conflicting.has(i's key)? FALSE (cleared when p advanced past i) -> Case B's (pre-this-fix) rule: '!conflicting.has(...)' is true -> ADVANCE past t too, UNCONDITIONALLY -- Case B never once compares compareRank(t,p) directly. Final: [i,t,p] = "itp".
handTrace.theBug: compareRank(t,p) = t.r - p.r = 3-2 = +1, NOT negative -- t does NOT outrank p. By the SAME rank-consistency logic Case A/the fixed-Case-C already use elsewhere, p should NOT have been forced past t in orderB -- p should have stopped BEFORE t (matching orderA's "ipt" result). Case B's group-inheritance blindly propagated i's OWN (valid, correctly rank-decided) resolution onto t, a DIFFERENT node with NO direct rank relationship established between it and p at all. i's loss to p says nothing about whether t (which merely happens to anchor onto i) should also lose to p -- t and i are NOT the same author's contiguous run here; they are two structurally-unrelated concurrent operations that happen to chain.
handTrace.generalPrinciple: Refines R0008's own general principle. R0008: an anchor lying OUTSIDE the current scan's walked region (`scanned`) is not safely skippable without a rank check. R0009 shows the boundary is subtler: an anchor being INSIDE `scanned` is not sufficient either, when the specific comparison that put it there was between a DIFFERENT pair (i vs p) than the pair actually in question (t vs p). Case B's group-inheritance assumes any node chained onto an already-resolved node shares that resolution's fate -- true for a genuine single-author contiguous run (where every member necessarily shares the SAME replica id as its anchor, so rank is automatically consistent), false when the chain crosses an authorship/replica boundary.

status: FIXED (2026-09-03), then SUPERSEDED (2026-09-05, see R0010). Fix: Case B's advance decision is now gated on `compareRank(other, node) < 0` in addition to the existing group-membership test -- see engine.ts's integrate(), the Case B branch comment citing this correction (part 2 of the same Engine Spec §6.2 sub-case iii-d correction R0008 is part 1 of). Hand-traced before implementation to confirm it does NOT reintroduce RFC NQ-2's interleaving problem: for a genuine single-author contiguous run, every member shares its anchor's own replica id, so the new check is automatically satisfied whenever the group's anchor already won -- it only changes behavior when a chain crosses an authorship/replica boundary, which isn't really one run to begin with. Verified via: this entry's own repro (5 replica-id combinations, exhaustive delivery orders); a hand-built same-author-chain-swept-by-a-competitor probe (contiguity preserved); a cross-replica-chain probe (still converges); a depth-2 chain crossing an authorship boundary partway through (converges, split occurs exactly at the boundary); all 22 adversarial cases; all worked traces; all 5 property suites; a 30,000-trial immediate-delivery fuzz run. Also hunted explicitly for a third instance of this bug shape in Case A -- confirmed architecturally immune, since Case A always performs a DIRECT pairwise rank comparison and never inherits a decision from group membership the way Case B did. (Ironically, a THIRD instance was later found anyway -- not in Case A, but one level ABOVE all three branches: R0010's transitivity-of-relative-order finding, reachable even with this fix and R0008's both active and individually correct at every step.) *** UPDATE 2026-09-05: given three bugs in the same decision procedure (R0008, R0009, R0010), `integrate()` was REPLACED OUTRIGHT with a faithful port of the real, published YATA algorithm rather than patched a third time -- see R0010's own status field and CLAUDE.md's 'Engine Spec §4.3 replaced by the real YATA algorithm (R0010)' entry. This entry's own repro was re-verified (all 3 causally-valid delivery-order permutations) against the NEW algorithm and converges correctly (to 'itp', consistently). *** Permanently retained in this corpus per Test Plan §2.3 Rule 2. Full writeup: CLAUDE.md's "Engine Spec §6.2 sub-case iii-d correction" entry (R0008/R0009) and the "Engine Spec §4.3 replaced by the real YATA algorithm (R0010)" entry (the current, real algorithm).
